about: My dog, my best friend for three years, from college until I joined the army. One Genie 4 session. First person as the dog: the camera is the dog's eyes, low, its snout and paws at the bottom of the frame, so the man it loves is always a full-body figure in the landscape. Kurosawa's staging (deep wide frames, small figures, wind and weather doing the acting) with Deakins's light (backlit silhouettes, layered mist, one warm light far away).
world: First-person view of a dog: the camera is a black-and-tan German Shepherd's eyes, sixty centimetres above the wet grass, its snout and front paws at the bottom of the frame; it never rises to human height and never cuts. Dawn in a remote mountain valley by a still lake. Thirty metres ahead on the stony shore stands its best friend: a lone young Black man in his early twenties, full body, back to us, a dark silhouette against bright mist, in a dark wool peacoat over a grey hooded college sweatshirt, jeans and work boots, an olive army duffel bag at his feet. On the left a small secluded log cabin, dark and empty: his family is gone. Across the lake under steep pine mountains, a small town with a church steeple and a few warm lights, half lost in mist. Wide, deep-focus, still, like Akira Kurosawa; soft backlight, layered mist and restrained cool colour like Roger Deakins. Wind in the grass, birds, lapping water.
beats: Mist drifts slowly across the lake; the man stands perfectly still at the water's edge, a dark silhouette, his back to the dog.
Wind rises off the lake: the tall grass bends in waves and the mist tears open, revealing the small town and its church steeple across the water.
The man turns his head and looks back at the empty cabin, its dark windows and the cold porch; nobody is there.
The man turns around, kneels on one knee in the grass and opens his arms; the dog runs to him across the wet grass.
Close in the dog's view: the man's hands hold the dog's head, his face in silhouette against the pale sky, breath steaming.
The man stands, lifts the olive army duffel onto his shoulder and walks away along the shore toward the distant town; the dog follows at his side, both small full-body silhouettes in the mist.
